source_name: Arzinger — Press centre / publications (Financial sector practice)
why_relevant: Ukrainian-language-first firm publishing on financial-services topics including advertising rules for financial services and antitrust risk — covers regulatory edges (AMCU, consumer/advertising) that pure banking sources miss. Practice page confirms bank/financial-group client base.

source_name: INTEGRITES — Publications (uk/en)
why_relevant: Publishes AML/financial-monitoring rule-change explainers in Ukrainian with an English mirror (/en/publications/). Financial monitoring is the compliance-deadline-dense corner of the UA banking rulebook and is under-covered by FX-focused firms.

source_name: Lexology — Ukraine banking & payments firm-update aggregator
why_relevant: Single highest-yield pointer for this cell: aggregates client alerts from many UA and international firms in one searchable stream, surfacing firms that never appeared in general web search. Also runs a 'Payment services: key compliance updates' periodic roundup (Lexology Pro) which is deadline-tracker-shaped.

source_name: Mondaq — Financial Services / Ukraine
why_relevant: Second, partially non-overlapping syndication network for UA firm briefings (e.g. open-banking analyses). Useful redundancy when a firm syndicates to Mondaq but not Lexology, and a cheap way to detect new firms entering the UA fintech-advisory space.

source_name: Chambers and Partners — Banking Regulation 2026, Ukraine chapter (Law & Practice / Trends and Developments)
why_relevant: Annually refreshed, firm-authored country chapter that states the regulatory architecture and the year's pipeline in one place. The 'Trends and Developments' half is where advisers flag drafts and expected effective dates — a near-ideal annual baseline for an A3 workstream.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters — Briefings (Ukraine)
why_relevant: Regional legal-market outlet that republishes CEE/UA firm briefings (Avellum's NBU currency-control notes appeared here) and reports on firm moves. Doubles as an actor-map maintainer: which firms staff Ukrainian banking/fintech practices.

source_name: Юридична Газета (yur-gazeta.com) — Банківське та фінансове право section
why_relevant: Ukrainian legal-trade newspaper that publishes practitioner bylines from exactly the firms in this cell (e.g. the payments-market analysis 'Платіжна реальність, яка захопила Україну') and covers rankings/firm moves. The best uk-language route into adviser commentary that never gets an English translation.

source_name: LIGA360 / ЛІГА:ЗАКОН — topic stream 'Фінансові та платіжні послуги'
why_relevant: A dated, day-by-day Ukrainian topic feed on financial and payment services that mixes regulator news with adviser commentary (biz.ligazakon.net). Its date-addressable URLs make it an efficient backfill and change-detection pointer for the whole cell.

source_name: Дебет-Кредит (news.dtkt.ua) — bank system / financial services news
why_relevant: Ukrainian accounting/finance professional outlet that reports NBU DRAFT regulations (e.g. draft governance requirements for payment service providers) at the consultation stage — earlier in the lifecycle than most firm alerts, and in plain Ukrainian.

source_name: Ukrainian Law Firms (ukrainianlawfirms.com) — annual handbook of leading firms
why_relevant: Actor-map source rather than a content source: an annual directory of Ukrainian firms with practice profiles, letting the cell enumerate every firm with a banking/finance or fintech practice instead of relying on the five seed names. Pair with Legal500 and Chambers UA rankings.

source_name: European Business Association (EBA Ukraine) / American Chamber of Commerce in Ukraine — member firm content & committees
why_relevant: Business associations host banking/financial-services committees where member advisers (Baker McKenzie, Big-4) circulate regulatory positions and comment on NBU drafts. Republishes member-firm news; a route to consultation-stage adviser positions that never appear as public alerts.

source_name: European Commission — Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood: Ukraine country page
why_relevant: Master hub for Ukraine accession documents: annual Enlargement Report + country SWD, screening process news, cluster/chapter opening milestones. Chapter 9 (Financial services) sits in Cluster 2 'Internal Market'; screening was reported completed Sep 2025. This is the canonical entry point for EU-set, forward-dated obligations on Ukrainian banks/PSPs.

source_name: EUR-Lex — Commission Staff Working Document, Ukraine Report (SWD(2025) 759 final)
why_relevant: The annual Ukraine country report is the single densest statement of what Ukraine must still align (CRR/CRD, BRRD, DGSD, capital markets acquis) and how prepared it is. EUR-Lex gives stable CELEX identifiers, making year-on-year diffing of the financial-services chapter mechanical.

source_name: Пульс Угоди (Association Agreement implementation monitoring system, CabMin)
why_relevant: Task-level, dated tracker of Association Agreement implementation across ~24 areas, incl. financial services; reportedly >2,000 tasks and ~7,500 measures with named executors. Best structured Ukrainian-language view of which EU directive-transposition tasks are due, late, or done.

source_name: Cabinet of Ministers — European integration / Association Agreement section
why_relevant: Hosts the Agreement text with Annex XVII/Annexes listing directives to be approximated and their deadlines, plus the monitoring-system description. Pointer into ministry-level obligation lists for financial services.

source_name: eu-ua.kmu.gov.ua — Ukrainian government European integration portal (annual AA implementation reports)
why_relevant: Publishes the annual 'Звіт про виконання Угоди про асоціацію' PDFs (2023, 2024, 2025 observed), which contain per-sector narrative on payment services authorisation, open banking, consumer protection in financial services and remaining gaps.

source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — European Integration page
why_relevant: NBU coordinates negotiating Chapter 9 'Financial services'. This page and NBU news carry the internal EU-integration plan, EBA/EIOPA/ECB cooperation, CRD/CRR transposition regulations and equivalence work (e.g. professional-secrecy equivalence bill for EBA assessment). Mirrored in uk at bank.gov.ua/ua/.

source_name: European Payments Council — Criteria for the extension of the SEPA geographical scope
why_relevant: The formal, EPC-Board-approved criteria a non-EEA community (i.e. Ukraine) must satisfy to enter SEPA scheme geographic scope, plus the periodic continuous-compliance review. Defines the exact conditions driving Ukraine's AML/PSD-alignment legislative package.

source_name: EPC List of SEPA Scheme Countries (EPC409-09, versioned PDF)
why_relevant: Authoritative, version-numbered list of countries/territories inside SEPA scheme scope. The moment Ukraine appears (v8.0 dated 2025-12 observed as latest), that is the decisive, machine-detectable signal of SEPA admission — far more reliable than press reporting.

source_name: EPC Register of Participants (SCT/SCT Inst/SDD/VOP scheme adherence)
why_relevant: Once Ukraine is in scope, individual Ukrainian PSP adherence appears in the EPC Register of Participants — the granular indicator of which banks actually go live in SEPA schemes, and in which order. Commercially the highest-value single dataset in this cell.

source_name: ECB — Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) pages / SEPA governance
why_relevant: ECB is the SEPA policy authority and (via the Euro Retail Payments Board and its oversight role) shapes conditions for third-country participation and euro-payments access. Also the venue for ECB Opinions on national legislation and for correspondent/TARGET access questions relevant to Ukraine.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — Memoranda of Understanding with third-country supervisors
why_relevant: An NBU–SSM MoU (or its absence) is a hard indicator of supervisory-convergence progress and of whether EU parent banks' Ukrainian subsidiaries can be supervised on a consolidated basis. Page is an authoritative, low-noise list.

source_name: European Banking Authority — publications, press releases and equivalence/confidentiality assessments
why_relevant: EBA assesses third-country professional-secrecy/confidentiality equivalence — a precondition NBU is explicitly legislating for. EBA guidelines also define the technical standards Ukraine transposes. Direct source for EU-side timing of an equivalence decision.

source_name: Ukraine Facility Plan portal (Ministry of Economy)
why_relevant: The Ukraine Plan 2024–2027 attaches money to dated, numbered reform indicators, several in the financial sector and EU-alignment space; quarterly disbursement conditionality makes these the most enforceable forward-dated deadlines in the country. Reporting indicates the indicator count rose from 146 to 173 and deadlines were shifted.

source_name: European Commission — Ukraine Facility (funding & conditionality)
why_relevant: EU-side counterpart to the Ukrainian portal: Commission assessments of whether quarterly indicators were met, amendments to the Plan, and disbursement decisions. Gives the authoritative pass/fail on reform deadlines rather than the Ukrainian self-assessment.

source_name: Ministry of Finance of Ukraine — Association Agreement implementation section
why_relevant: MoF co-owns approximation for capital markets, accounting/audit, insurance and public finance parts of the financial-services acquis (with NSSMC and NBU). Publishes its own implementation reporting and draft-law pipeline.

source_name: Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture — quarterly AA implementation monitoring publications
why_relevant: Publishes quarterly monitoring of the AA action plan (e.g. Q1 2025 report observed), covering trade-in-services and establishment commitments that bracket financial services. Useful for cadence and for naming responsible executors.

source_name: EEAS / Council — EU-Ukraine Association Agenda and Association Council conclusions
why_relevant: The Association Agenda is the negotiated short-list of priority reforms, and Association Council / Association Committee in Trade Configuration outcomes formally record financial-services commitments and their timing. The 10th Association Council met 9 Apr 2025.
